metadata.title: KP08 · Laplacian Eigenmaps
metadata.description: Reasoning-led 2.3.1; editable native teaching deck; global manual mode; no narration.

neighbors-title.name: neighbors-title
neighbors-title.text: Which local relationships should an embedding preserve?

neighbors-context.name: neighbors-context
neighbors-context.text: Compare actual distances to radius $\epsilon=1.5$. This example uses unit edge weights, distinct from edge lengths.

neighbors-source.name: neighbors-source
neighbors-source.text: PR · KP08 · 1/10  |  Handout §1,§2,§3  |  Manual Next / Prev

neighbors-bubble.name: neighbors-bubble
neighbors-bubble.text: Verify pairwise distances before adding edges under one radius rule.

neighbors-heat.name: neighbors-heat
neighbors-heat.text: Alternative: $W_{ij}=e^{-d_{ij}^2/\sigma^2}$ on edges; zero for nonneighbors.

matrices-title.name: matrices-title
matrices-title.text: Derive adjacency, degree, and Laplacian matrices

matrices-context.name: matrices-context
matrices-context.text: $W$ is symmetric and nonnegative with zero diagonal; $D_{ii}=\sum_jW_{ij}$. Rows correspond to nodes.

matrices-source.name: matrices-source
matrices-source.text: PR · KP08 · 2/10  |  Handout §2,§3  |  Manual Next / Prev

matrices-bubble.name: matrices-bubble
matrices-bubble.text: Sum rows, then subtract entries; distinguish the two operations.

edge-loss-title.name: edge-loss-title
edge-loss-title.text: Write neighbor differences as a graph objective

edge-loss-context.name: edge-loss-context
edge-loss-context.text: $z_i$ is node i’s one-dimensional coordinate. Triangle positions depict adjacency rather than coordinate values. Both edges have unit weights.

edge-loss-source.name: edge-loss-source
edge-loss-source.text: PR · KP08 · 3/10  |  Handout §4  |  Manual Next / Prev

edge-loss-bubble.name: edge-loss-bubble
edge-loss-bubble.text: Square differences on each edge and account for symmetric double counting.

collapse-title.name: collapse-title
collapse-title.text: Does minimizing differences alone yield useful coordinates?

collapse-context.name: collapse-context
collapse-context.text: Keep the same two edges and weights while allowing arbitrary one-dimensional coordinates.

collapse-source.name: collapse-source
collapse-source.text: PR · KP08 · 4/10  |  Handout §4  |  Manual Next / Prev

collapse-bubble.name: collapse-bubble
collapse-bubble.text: Compare candidate edge costs and identify the missing condition.

constraint-context.name: constraint-context
constraint-context.text: Degrees are $D=\operatorname{diag}(1,2,1)$; centering and scale use degree weights.

constraint-source.name: constraint-source
constraint-source.text: PR · KP08 · 5/10  |  Handout §4,§5  |  Manual Next / Prev

constraint-bubble.name: constraint-bubble
constraint-bubble.text: Fix the weighted center and squared length; identify what each constraint excludes.

eigen-context.name: eigen-context
eigen-context.text: Exclude the constant direction, then minimize at fixed weighted scale; $\eta$ is a generalized eigenvalue.

eigen-source.name: eigen-source
eigen-source.text: PR · KP08 · 6/10  |  Handout §5  |  Manual Next / Prev

eigen-bubble.name: eigen-bubble
eigen-bubble.text: Differentiate with the scale constraint, then verify the example’s nontrivial direction.

eigen-derive.name: eigen-derive
eigen-derive.text: $\begin{gathered}\mathcal L=\mathbf z^TL\mathbf z-\eta(\mathbf z^TD\mathbf z-1)\\2L\mathbf z-2\eta D\mathbf z=0\\L\mathbf z=\eta D\mathbf z\end{gathered}$

eigen-verify.name: eigen-verify
eigen-verify.text: $\begin{gathered}\mathbf z=(-1,0,1)^T/\sqrt2\\L\mathbf z=\mathbf z=D\mathbf z,\quad\eta=1\\J=\mathbf z^TL\mathbf z=\eta\mathbf z^TD\mathbf z=\eta\end{gathered}$

components-title.name: components-title
components-title.text: If the graph disconnects, is there only one zero mode?

components-context.name: components-context
components-context.text: Use the same three nodes; the right graph loses its second edge. Positions depict connectivity rather than embedding coordinates.

components-source.name: components-source
components-source.text: PR · KP08 · 7/10  |  Handout §6  |  Manual Next / Prev

components-bubble.name: components-bubble
components-bubble.text: Locate regions that can take independent constants, then count zero modes.

numeric-form-title.name: numeric-form-title
numeric-form-title.text: Convert the problem to a symmetric eigenproblem

numeric-form-context.name: numeric-form-context
numeric-form-context.text: Require positive degrees. Diagonal entries of $D^{-1/2}$ are inverse square-root degrees.

numeric-form-source.name: numeric-form-source
numeric-form-source.text: PR · KP08 · 8/10  |  Handout §7  |  Manual Next / Prev

numeric-form-bubble.name: numeric-form-bubble
numeric-form-bubble.text: Track the normalized variable and convert back to degree-weighted coordinates.

numeric-form-constraint.name: numeric-form-constraint
numeric-form-constraint.text: $\begin{gathered}\mathbf u_0\propto D^{1/2}\mathbf1\\\mathbf u\perp\mathbf u_0\Leftrightarrow\mathbf z^TD\mathbf1=0\\\mathbf u^T\mathbf u=1\Rightarrow\mathbf z^TD\mathbf z=1\end{gathered}$

limits-title.name: limits-title
limits-title.text: Do node coordinates define a transform for new observations?

limits-context.name: limits-context
limits-context.text: The objective directly constrains edges; global distances and labels need validation. Compare two protocols with the same training graph and new point.

limits-source.name: limits-source
limits-source.text: PR · KP08 · 9/10  |  Handout §8  |  Manual Next / Prev

limits-bubble.name: limits-bubble
limits-bubble.text: Distinguish an extension rule from rebuilding the graph, and identify what the objective does not preserve.

limits-reembed.name: limits-reembed
limits-reembed.text:
Joint graph, re-embed
Declare transductive evaluation

limits-scope.name: limits-scope
limits-scope.text:
Sparse solvers, e.g. Lanczos:
cost depends on edges,
spectrum, and convergence.

new-path-title.name: new-path-title
new-path-title.text: Check a candidate embedding on a four-node path

new-path-context.name: new-path-context
new-path-context.text: Use a unit-weight path. Left-to-right node order is one through four; drawing positions encode adjacency order only.

new-path-source.name: new-path-source
new-path-source.text: PR · KP08 · 10/10  |  Handout §9  |  Manual Next / Prev

new-path-bubble.name: new-path-bubble
new-path-bubble.text: Compute weighted center, scale, and edge cost. How many zero modes follow if the middle edge is removed? Do constraints ensure optimality?

new-path-components.name: new-path-components
new-path-components.text: Cut middle edge → two components → two zero modes. Feasibility alone does not establish optimality.
